rationale: The printed entry and chapter identify the spiritual Egypt of Rev 11:8 (paired with Sodom) as Jerusalem, the city where the Lord was crucified and the killer of the prophets. This is the minimum claim that diverges from the common interpretation of Egypt as generic bondage/sin/world. The supplied cross-texts establish the identification more tightly than any rival: the explicit crime-scene clause 'where also our Lord was crucified' forces a Jerusalem referent; Isaiah already addresses Jerusalem as Sodom/Gomorrah; Galatians equates present Jerusalem with bondage; Matthew 23 and Rev 18:24 fix the blood of prophets there. Secondary elaborations that equate this Jerusalem-Egypt with the whore/Babylon of ch. 17–18, the seven-mountain western bloc, or the full Exodus–plagues typology are not required for the core and remain open to dispute. No counter-reading accounts for the same cluster of identifiers with fewer unsupported steps.
book_core_identification: Spiritually (in Rev 11:8), Egypt names Jerusalem—the city that kills the prophets and is the place 'where also our Lord was crucified.'
book_secondary_elaborations: The same city is the whore of Babylon that rides the beast (Rev 17–18).
She is the covenant priesthood gone serpentine (Aaron’s rod cast down).
She sits as the westernmost ('hindermost') seven-mountain power-bloc.
The entire Fall of Babylon is a scene-for-scene Exodus similitude culminating in the song of Moses.
strongest_counter_interpretation: Egypt in Rev 11:8 remains the conventional symbol of bondage to sin / the oppressive godless world-system (or, more narrowly, of any persecuting imperial city), while the relative clause 'where also our Lord was crucified' merely locates the witnesses’ bodies in historical Jerusalem without transferring the spiritual name Egypt onto Jerusalem itself; Sodom and Egypt function as ethical/typological labels for moral corruption and slavery rather than as proper names for the city.
counter_core_identification: Spiritual Egypt = bondage/world-system (or generic hostile power), not Jerusalem.
material_core_denial: The counter denies that the spiritual name Egypt is being applied to Jerusalem; it treats the crucifixion clause as geographic only and keeps Egypt as the traditional abstract symbol of enslavement.
counter_case: Mainstream Christian typology (Exod 1–14; Deut 5:6; 1 Cor 10; Heb 11) consistently equates Egypt with the house of slavery / the world of sin from which God delivers, not with the covenant city.

Rev 11:8 can be read as a double label: the great city is spiritually like Sodom and Egypt (corrupt and enslaving) and is also the place of the crucifixion, without requiring identity of the two descriptors.
Revelation elsewhere uses Babylon as the primary code-name for the hostile city, so Egypt need not be forced into the same referent.
Gal 4:25’s 'Jerusalem … in bondage' is an allegory of law versus promise, not a lexical redefinition of Egypt.
book_explanatory_advantages: Rev 11:8’s relative clause 'where also our Lord was crucified' is the only geographic datum that uniquely identifies one city; any reading that severs the spiritual names from that clause leaves the verse’s syntax under-motivated.
Isa 1:10 already applies 'Sodom/Gomorrah' directly to Jerusalem’s rulers, establishing the exact prophetic method of spiritual naming that John re-uses.
Gal 4:25 supplies the parallel 'bondage' language for 'Jerusalem which now is,' matching Egypt’s fixed title 'house of bondage.'
Matt 23:35–37 / Luke 13:33 and Rev 18:24 converge on Jerusalem as the unique repository of prophetic blood, completing the three-name set (Sodom, Egypt, Babylon) on a single referent.
The method is self-consistent with the book’s stated rule of multi-witness OT definitions rather than isolated NT novelty.
counter_explanatory_advantages: Preserves the broad, stable Christian consensus that Egypt = bondage/sin/world across Exodus typology and Pauline application.
Avoids collapsing multiple apocalyptic symbols (Sodom, Egypt, Babylon) into one historical city, which some readers find over-compressed.
Keeps open the possibility that 'the great city' in different chapters can shift referents (Rome, the world system, unfaithful Jerusalem) without forcing a single identity.
decisive_sources: Matthew 23:37 / Revelation 18:24 (prophetic blood fixed to Jerusalem)
Exodus 20:2 (Egypt = house of bondage, the title transferred)
unresolved_objections: Whether the Jerusalem identified as spiritual Egypt is also identical to the whore of Babylon that rides the seven-headed beast remains a secondary claim resting on further typology (Aaron’s rod, westernmost nation, full Exodus–vial parallels) not required by the core entry.
The precise historical or eschatological scope of that Jerusalem (first-century only, ongoing covenant-city, or future restoration) is left open by the supplied texts.
